hero.h1: Gas Line Installation in Highland Park, IL
hero.sub: Running a new gas line for a range, dryer, generator, fireplace or outdoor kitchen? Our plumbers are licensed for gas work, handle the permit and pressure-test every line before we call it done. Serving Highland Park and the North Shore.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber inspecting the gas meters and gas line connections in a basement

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.intro: We run new gas lines and extend existing ones for:

tiles.body: Switching from electric to gas, or moving the range in a kitchen remodel.
A dedicated line for a gas dryer in the basement or laundry room.
Standby generators need a line sized for their full load.
New gas fireplaces or wood-to-gas conversions. See [gas fireplace service](/highland-park/gas-fireplace).
Grills, fire pits and patio heaters on a permanent line instead of a propane tank.
Tankless units often need a larger line than the old tank. See [tankless water heaters](/highland-park/tankless-water-heater).

blocks.intro: Gas line work has to be right the first time. Here's how we handle it:

steps.body: We look at the appliance, the distance from the meter and your existing lines to size the new line correctly.
Most gas line work needs a permit. We handle it as part of the job, so you don't have to.
We run the line, make the connections and install shutoff valves where code requires them.
We pressure-test the line and check every connection before the appliance goes into service.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation in Older Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and about 1 in 4 before 1940. Adding a gas appliance to an older home usually means looking at more than the new run.

items.body: Many older homes still run on original black iron or steel gas piping. Before we tie a new line into it, we check the existing piping and fittings for corrosion and leaks.
A generator, tankless heater or outdoor kitchen can push an older system past what it was sized for. We check that your service can handle the new load.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Do you need a permit for gas line work in Illinois?
items.preview: Yes, most gas line work needs a permit. We handle it as part of the job.
items.answer: Yes, most gas line work needs a permit. A licensed plumber handles the permitting as part of the job, so you don't need to navigate it yourself. Permitted work also protects you when you sell your home.

items.q: Can I install a gas line myself?
items.preview: No. Gas line work should be done by a licensed pro.
items.answer: Gas line work should be done by a licensed pro. Gas line work requires specific tools, knowledge of local code and a pressure test that isn't available to unlicensed individuals. A DIY gas connection can create a hazard that doesn't show up right away.

items.q: How long does gas line installation take?
items.preview: A short run can take a few hours. Longer runs can take a day or more.
items.answer: A short run to a range or dryer can often be done in a few hours. Longer runs, generators or outdoor kitchens can take a full day or more. You'll get a realistic timeline before work begins.

items.q: How much does gas line installation cost?
items.preview: It depends on the run and the appliance. You get a flat rate before anything starts.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the run, the pipe size, the appliance, permits and access. We don't price gas work over the phone. A licensed technician looks at the job and gives you a flat rate before anything starts.
